During a media scrum about an hour before her death, teenager Silke Bischoff is held hostage at gunpoint following an unsuccessful bank robbery. Cologne, Germany. 1988

The Gladbeck hostage crisis was a hostage taking event in August 1988 after a bank robbery in Gladbeck, Germany. Two men went on the run for two days through Germany and the Netherlands while holding many different people hostage. The situation was put to an end in a police operation on the A3 motorway on August 18. Three people were killed during this crisis.

On August 16, after the bank robbery, the robbers took two clerks hostage and demanded a car and ransom money. After several hours of negotiations, the abductors were given 300,000 DM and a white Audi 100 as a getaway car.

On August 17, in Bremen, the abductors hijacked a public-transit bus with 32 passengers. The media interviewed the abductors and the hostages without any interference from the police. The two bank clerks were released there. Police arrested the girlfriend of one of the robbers, who they had stopped to puck up along the way, when she got off the bus to use the washroom. The robbers then threatened to kill a hostage every 5 minutes and, after the expiration of the ultimatum, they shot a 15-year-old Italian boy in the head. The girlfriend was about to be released but arrived too late because of a broken handcuff key.

On August 18, the robbers were given a BMW 735i which had been prepared so that the engine could be stopped by remote control. Taking teenager Silke Bischoff with them, the robbers drove to a pedestrian area where they were interviewed by the media. Here is a video of the robbers, the girlfriend and Bischoff being interviewed.

Shortly thereafter, after the police discovered that they had misplaced the remote to disable the car, a police car crashed into the getaway car, which led to a gunfight and the death of Bischoff.

The robbers were arrested and given life sentences while the girlfriend received 24 years.
